unsupported: Dakota Timber Company operates from Horace, North Dakota, where it produces a line of reclaimed wood products for residential and commercial projects.
The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but its roots are tied to the upper Midwest's agricultural heritage.
The shop manufactures fireplace mantels, floating shelf kits, structural beams, shiplap paneling, stair treads, brackets, and custom tops.
Lumber is sourced primarily from decommissioned agricultural buildings across the upper Midwest and from urban tree removals, then milled and finished in-house.
Production is made-to-order with a typical lead time of four to six weeks, and finished goods ship via LTL freight.
Customers include homeowners, builders, and interior designers across the region.

Recent project work includes floating shelf installations for Rachel Platt of RP at Home, a fireplace mantel for D Gilpin Properties, white oak shiplap for Klein Custom Homes, and a whole-home package for Studio West's Rose Creek residence in Fargo, North Dakota.
The company positions its output as 100 percent American-made, emphasizing low-impact production and the reuse of materials that would otherwise enter the waste stream.
Its floating shelf kits feature a proprietary mounting bracket designed for straightforward installation.
Known for: 100% Made in America; Lumber sourced from agricultural buildings and urban tree removals; Custom made-to-order production; 4-6 week lead time; Proprietary floating shelf mounting bracket
